| FE-163 | **"Where is my fear?"** "A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear? says the Lord of hosts to you, O priests, who despise my name." The answer given: "By offering polluted food upon my altar … By saying that the Lord's table may be despised" | **Meaning:** God names himself as father and master, and asks for both honour and fear. The lack is shown in what the priests do at the altar and say about it. **Implies:** this one verse states, in God's own words, a father to be honoured and a master to be feared. It bears on FE-140 (1Pe 1:17 and Rom 8:15), which I had set side by side as my own pairing. | Mal 1:6–7 | S | 10.9; **11 §4** (with FE-140) | **W / RS** |

| FE-164 | **A covenant of fear.** "My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him. It was a covenant of fear, and he feared me. He stood in awe of my name. True instruction was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many from iniquity" | **Meaning:** the covenant with Levi is named as one of life and peace, and as one of fear. The fear is stated together with true instruction, lips without wrong, walking with God, and turning many from iniquity. Unit 1 (FE-33) already cites Mal 2:5 through the *yārēʾ* (to fear) words. This hit is the noun in the same verse. **Implies:** "life" is a life-side word, and it is held. | Mal 2:5–6 | S | 10.9, 10.5 (lips); life side → OT-08 | **D** (FE-33); **W** (2:6); **H (OT-08)** |

| FE-165 | **"Great deeds of terror", and what they were for.** "by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and by great deeds of terror, all of which the Lord your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes? To you it was shown, that you might know that the Lord is God; there is no other besides him"; the same words in the confession at the firstfruits (Deu 26:8), at Moses' death (Deu 34:12), and in Jeremiah's prayer: "with a strong hand and outstretched arm, and with great terror" | **Meaning:** the word names God's deeds at the Exodus (face F). Deu 4:35 states their purpose: "that you might know". **Implies:** the terror word stands with "a mighty hand and an outstretched arm" in all four verses. This bears on OT-06 (God's hand). | Deu 4:34–35; Deu 26:8; Deu 34:12; Jer 32:21 | S | 10.2 (knowing), 10.9; **OT-06** | **W**; signpost to OT-06 |
